jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer I - Global KYC and Onboarding
jobs.description:
Wise is a global technology company, building the best way to move and manage the world’s money.

Min fees. Max ease. Full speed.

Whether people and businesses are sending money to another country, spending abroad, or making and receiving international payments, Wise is on a mission to make their lives easier and save them money.

As part of our team, you will be helping us create an entirely new network for the world's money.

For everyone, everywhere.

More about our mission and what we offer.

We are currently only considering local candidates as relocation support is not provided for this role. For local candidates we are able to support transfer of visa sponsorship.

We are the Global KYC and Onboarding squad in the Servicing department and we have a mission: to enable teams at Wise to expand and fine-tune the business in a "config change" manner all across the globe, while remaining compliant and safe for the customers. There are three teams in the squad: Business Onboarding Verification, Personal Onboarding Verification and Wise Platform Verification (our B2B platform).

The scale we operate at: In FY2025, 15.6 million people and businesses used Wise, we onboarded over 5.9 million new customers (~500k/month), and moved £145.2bn across borders (~£400m/day) across 160+ countries and 40+ currencies. Our verification systems aren't supporting tools — they're core production infrastructure that protects customers, enables growth, and must stay reliable under constant change in regulations, policies, and evolving threat patterns.

All of the teams are diverse, cross-functional groups passionate about solving complex problems with elegant solutions. We bring together backend and frontend engineers, mobile developers, designers, data analysts, and product managers who collaborate closely to deliver exceptional customer experiences. Our teams are responsible for the critical verification journeys that business and personal customers complete before using Wise's products. We own the entire verification lifecycle – from document collection flows and automated review systems to agent tooling and compliance monitoring. We operate with high ownership in a bottom-up, transparent culture, make data-driven decisions, and celebrate both technical excellence and customer impact. Right now we're focused on building KYC/FinCrime as a configuration-driven product, refactoring and building new scalable microservice systems, and increasing automation using ML/AI where it genuinely improves decisioning, review quality, and operational efficiency — with safe fallbacks and clear observability. As a team that touches both regulatory requirements and customer experience, we have unique opportunities to innovate in a space traditionally resistant to change.

By joining one of our teams, you'll directly impact these customers by transforming a traditionally frustrating experience into one that's fast, intuitive, and fair. Your code will help individuals and small businesses access global banking faster, enable entrepreneurs to pay international employees on time, and allow people like you and your teammates support their families across borders without friction. We're not just building verification systems – we're removing barriers that stand between our customers and their financial freedom.

We need like-minded engineers in all the teams in the squad, so we'll use the interview process to discover where your unique skills shine brightest. Ultimately, we want to match you with the team that perfectly aligns with your experience and sets you up for success!

As a Senior Software Engineer, you will own large-sized, impactful projects within the domain. Your responsibilities span end-to-end:

-
You will own the technical roadmap for your areas of ownership, ensuring they address important technical debt, reliability, scalability, and security concerns.

-
You will be instrumental in designing and implementing robust backend systems that provide clean APIs and interfaces to hide the internal complexity.

-
You will drive the integration with various risk and mitigation systems to ensure that Wise is compliant.

-
You will take initiative to identify and solve impactful problems both within your team and beyond, contributing to high-impact cross-team initiatives.

What we expect from you:

-
You have 4+ years of experience working with Java 8+, Spring framework, asynchronous message queues (e.g., Kafka, RabbitMQ), and have architected and built highly scalable microservices.

-
A strong product mindset and a deep passion for both customer experience and regulatory compliance.

-
You will prioritize work with a holistic view of the customer and business impact, making data-driven decisions to solve complex, ambiguous problems.

-
Exceptional communication skills, with the ability to articulate complex technical and architectural concepts clearly to diverse audiences, including product managers, designers, and other engineering teams.

-
You demonstrate a commitment to writing clean, testable, maintainable, and highly performant code, and you are a strong advocate for best coding practices and rigorous code reviews.

-
Proven ability to identify and lead the technical delivery of large-scale, organisationally-complex projects, adept at anticipating and escalating organizational blockers.

-
Extensive experience working with relational and non-relational databases, including advanced query optimization, schema design, and data lifecycle management for sensitive information.

What does success look like?

-
You’ll have deeply embedded yourself within our mission, owning and delivering quarterly goals for the team, significantly impacting our ability to scale and improve verification processes.

-
You’ll own the technical roadmap for your areas, ensuring it supports both immediate delivery needs and long-term strategic objectives, including addressing technical debt and improving system health.

-
You’ll leverage your expertise to identify the right solutions to solve ambiguous, open-ended problems, driving tough prioritization decisions that deliver clear business and customer value.

-
You’ll consistently define and implement technical solutions or efficient operational processes that level up your team and contribute beyond it, mentoring other engineers and sharing best practices.

-
You’ll inspire a high-performing team environment where ideas are shared, technical excellence is pursued, and continuous learning is embraced.

jobs.title: Head of Global Partnerships - Cards
jobs.description:

You'll own the partnerships that underpin both how customers spend with Wise and how they pay Wise. Your decisions will shape the future of the Wise Card, our card funding capabilities, and the commercial partnerships that support millions of customers around the world.

This isn't a traditional partnerships role. You'll own Wise's global strategy across Visa, Mastercard, and our acquiring partners, ensuring they enable our mission. You'll shape how we launch the Wise Card into new markets, how customers fund their Wise Account using cards, and how we build commercial partnerships that improve customer outcomes while strengthening the economics of our global card programmes.

You'll work across Product, Banking & Expansion, Treasury, Finance, Compliance, Legal and Engineering to solve complex problems and help Wise continue to scale globally.

Your mission:

Own Wise's global card partnerships:

- Own our executive relationships with Visa, Mastercard, our issuer banking partners and strategic acquiring partners. Define how Wise works with these organisations globally, aligning commercial strategy, product priorities and expansion goals to create long-term competitive advantage.

- You'll represent Wise in commercial negotiations, product forums and strategic planning, while ensuring our partnerships continue to support Wise's ambitious growth plans globally.

Build and scale the world's best global card programme:

- Define the strategy for Wise's global card programmes across issuing and card acceptance.

- Lead complex commercial negotiations covering network economics, incentives, issuer partnerships, acquiring relationships and long-term commercial frameworks. Own the commercial models that underpin our card business and continually improve the economics of how customers spend with Wise and fund their Wise Account.

- You'll be equally comfortable negotiating a multi-year commercial agreement, reviewing an issuer agreement with Legal, supporting due diligence for a new BIN sponsor or working through scheme documentation to enable a new card feature.

Enable global expansion:

- Partner with regional Banking & Expansion teams to launch the Wise Card into new markets and new legal entities.

- Work directly with regional Visa and Mastercard teams and local partners to define market strategy, remove blockers and accelerate launches. You'll understand that successful expansion requires balancing global consistency with local market realities and you'll enjoy getting into the details to make things happen.

Build compliant, scalable card programmes:

- Work closely with Compliance, Financial Crime and Legal teams to ensure our card partnerships and programmes remain compliant as Wise scales.

- You'll understand how scheme rules, AML and financial crime requirements, issuer obligations and local regulation intersect, and you'll work directly with partners to solve regulatory challenges that enable launches rather than slow them down.

- You're comfortable owning regulatory conversations with external partners and know that strong commercial partnerships are built on strong compliance foundations.

Be Wise's card ecosystem expert:

- Become the company's go-to expert on the global card ecosystem.

- You'll understand the technical, operational and commercial detail behind card schemes, issuer processing, acquiring, settlement, interchange, network economics, certification, digital wallets and payment acceptance.

- You'll use that expertise to influence product strategy, advise Engineering and Product teams, and identify new opportunities for Wise to improve the customer experience.

This role will give you the opportunity to:

-
Own some of Wise's most strategic external partnerships and represent Wise with senior leaders across Visa, Mastercard, issuer banks and global acquiring partners.

-
Shape the future of one of Wise's fastest-growing products by influencing how the Wise Card expands globally.

-
Lead commercial negotiations that directly improve customer outcomes and the economics of Wise's global card programmes.

-
Work on complex international launches, partnering with regional teams to bring new card products and payment capabilities to market.

-
Solve difficult commercial, technical and regulatory challenges across multiple markets where no playbook exists.

-
Define how Wise partners with the global card ecosystem for the next decade while remaining hands-on in making that strategy a reality.

The Americas L&D Specialist owns Fraud L&D outcomes across the Americas region and holds a global horizontal scope: measurement operations & insight - the shared L1-L3 tooling all specialists use, L4 attribution execution, data partnerships and knowledge governance.

The L&D Lead owns the measurement architecture as a strategic system and the L4-L5 impact & ROI narrative to stakeholders. The Americas specialist runs the operational cycles that feed it.

The role sits inside a three-specialist regional model. Each specialist carries the same shared regional scope for their region and one distinct horizontal owned globally on behalf of the Fraud L&D team.

Specialists are not expected to deliver every in-person onboarding session themselves. They design the training, deploy and manage a regional pool of trainers and mentors to deliver it, and step in to facilitate themselves when capacity allows or when the session requires it (e.g. new content, high-risk topics, cover). Ownership of the outcome sits with the specialist; delivery is shared with the trainer & mentor pool.

Measurement operations

Owns the shared L1–L3 tooling all three regional specialists use for their own delivery: assessment templates, quiz banks, feedback instruments, Kirkpatrick L1–L3 reporting templates. Each regional specialist runs L1–L3 in region using this shared toolkit. Also owns the operational LNA and RCA cadence and templates the team applies. Runs the L4 attribution cycles globally for defined interventions: pre-baseline → post-measurement at 30/60/90 days → comparison group. Publishes results. Feeds outputs to the L&D Lead, who owns the L4–L5 impact & ROI narrative to stakeholders.

Data partnerships & L&D analytics

Day-to-day point of contact with QC and analytics teams for L&D data plumbing. Maintains the L&D Lightdash dashboards (speed-to-competency, DA%, cohort performance). Translates QC and DA data into learning-needs insights the team acts on. Escalates framework-level data-partnership decisions to the L&D Lead.

Knowledge governance

Owns the operational L&D↔KM link: versioning, review cycles, wikis and updates-channel sync between training content and operational knowledge. Standardises ownership and review cycles across L&D and KM so regional specialists and Ops leads work from one source of truth.

Technical Scoping & Discovery: Take ownership of broad, ambiguous problem spaces. Uncover hidden challenges, propose robust architectural designs, and execute your own roadmap.

jobs.description:
Wise is a global technology company, building the best way to move and manage the world’s money.

More about our mission and what we offer.

As a Financial Risk Manager, you will be the principal second-line Financial Risk specialist supporting Wise’s Brazilian operations and legal entities, with opportunities to contribute to Financial Risk matters across LATAM.

This is a Level 5 individual-contributor role combining independent risk oversight with hands-on technical delivery. You will assess and quantify financial exposures, maintain the local Risk and Capital Management framework, support prudential reporting and produce the analysis required for senior management, local governance bodies and regulatory decision-making.

The role requires a detailed understanding of how money moves through Wise Pagamentos, Wise Corretora and relevant Wise group entities, including the accounts, ledgers, counterparties, currencies, settlement mechanisms and regulatory obligations involved.

Your mission

As the regional risk manager you will be responsible for:

-
Provide independent second-line oversight and challenge of liquidity, funding, intraday liquidity, settlement, counterparty credit, concentration, FX, market, safeguarding, capital and intercompany risks.

-
Maintain and continue developing Wise Brazil’s Risk and Capital Management framework, policies, risk appetite metrics, limits, KRIs and governance reporting.

-
Prepare, coordinate or independently challenge capital plans, capital forecasts, RWA calculations and financial risk stress-testing exercises.

-
Translate Finance forecasts from Group assumptions and IFRS-based information into risk analysis appropriate for the Brazilian entities and COSIF-based prudential framework.

-
Support the completeness, accuracy and timely submission of applicable prudential and Financial Risk reports, including DDR, DRM, DLO, DLI, DRL, Pilar 3 and other relevant BCB reporting.

-
Monitor capital adequacy, regulatory and internal limits, concentration exposures, liquidity positions and end-of-day FX positions, escalating actual or forecast breaches.

-
Analyse BRL liquidity across normal and closed-market periods, including nights, weekends and holidays, and assess the impact of payment-rail, banking-partner or funding constraints.

-
Define, review and backtest liquidity and safeguarding buffers using historical data, forward-looking volumes and credible stress scenarios.

-
Assess new products, banking arrangements, safeguarding structures and financial infrastructure by reconstructing the legal-entity and funds flow and quantifying the resulting exposures.

-
Evaluate the financial and prudential implications of payment systems like Pix, SPI, STR in Brazil, SPEI in Mexico among other LatAm payment systems, FX and settlement arrangements, including cut-offs, prefunding, trapped liquidity and operational concentration.

-
Perform counterparty and concentration analysis for banks, liquidity providers, safeguarding institutions and other financial partners.

-
Challenge Finance, Treasury, PayOps, Banking, Product and Engineering on financial assumptions, control design, data quality, reconciliation and remediation plans.

-
Convert Financial Risk analysis into practical recommendations such as limits, launch conditions, liquidity controls, capital actions, counterparty diversification and contingency arrangements.

-
Prepare clear recommendations and escalation materials for the Brazilian CRO and CFO, local Risk Committee, Board and other governance forums.

-
Support Compliance and senior management in technical prudential engagements with Regulators.

-
Monitor regulatory developments affecting capital, liquidity, safeguarding, FX, concentration and prudential reporting, assessing their quantitative and operational impact.

-
Collaborate with global Financial Risk teams while ensuring that Brazilian legal-entity and regulatory requirements remain appropriately addressed.
jobs.requirements_raw:

-
Understanding of Brazilian prudential accounting and reporting, including COSIF and applicable BCB reports.

-
Experience analysing payment and FX flows across multiple legal entities, accounts and settlement mechanisms.

-
Ability to turn complex financial analysis into clear decisions, launch conditions and senior governance recommendations.

About the Role

As a KYC Operations Associate Analyst, you'll be at the forefront of ensuring Wise adheres to the highest regulatory and compliance standards. You'll play a crucial role in protecting our customers and maintaining the integrity of our platform by conducting thorough customer due diligence, analyzing customer activities, and meticulously maintaining our KYC records. If you're eager to develop your career in the KYC domain, this is the perfect opportunity to make a real impact!

What You’ll Do

-
Customer and Business Onboarding: Dive into initial and ongoing Customer Due Diligence (CDD) and Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) reviews. You’ll make critical risk-based decisions, ensuring our risk mitigation standards are met. You’ll also get to collect, analyze, and verify customer information against KYC/AML guidelines, gaining a deep understanding of potential risks associated with various customer types. This involves assessing everything from customer identity documents and online company registries to complex business structures, ultimate beneficial ownership, and customer source of wealth documentation, plus adverse media screening.

-
Transaction Monitoring and Periodic Reviews: You’ll review customer transaction history, providing key insights into customer behavior patterns that could indicate risks. You'll also conduct periodic reviews, analyzing changes in customer history and account usage to keep us one step ahead.

-
Documentation and Record Keeping: Accuracy is key! You’ll ensure customer records are not only accurate but also updated as required. You’ll maintain organized and detailed records of customers and the decisions made during the KYC process, all while complying with data privacy regulations and internal data security protocols.

-
Risk Assessment and Escalation: You’ll perform and document customer risk assessments based on the information you gather. When you identify activities that exceed our internal risk tolerance, you’ll escalate them to the relevant teams. You’ll also be vigilant in identifying potential money laundering and fraudulent activities, filing Suspicious Activity Reports with proper documentation and rationale.

-
Customer Communication: You’ll communicate effectively with customers through various channels (phone, email, and chat), providing top-notch service and support.

-
KPIs and More: You'll perform your tasks within the expected key performance indicators set by the leadership team, and you'll tackle other position-related tasks assigned by your lead. You’ll also participate in meetings, training, and internal and external events, contributing to our collaborative environment.

Your primary purpose is to ensure the effective mitigation of financial crime risks associated with Wise's customers, while maintaining a strong focus on operational efficiency, regulatory compliance and a customer-centric approach. You will foster a high-performing team, drive operational excellence, and act as a subject matter expert in KYC/AML/Fraud/Screening and financial crime prevention. You will be responsible for ensuring your team meets performance targets, maintains or elevates quality standards, and contributes to a culture of continuous improvement within the FinCrime Operations organization.

The FinCrime Operations Team Lead is a dual-focused leader, combining strong people leadership with domain and operational expertise. You will be instrumental in building and refining processes that prioritise customer impact while maintaining focus on the evolving risks within the financial services industry, specific product vulnerabilities, and the requirements set by regulations and partners. This includes supporting the development of compliant and scalable processes and possessing an understanding of financial crime risks associated with our customers, products, and tooling.

Job Responsibilities

-
Team Leadership

You will lead by example, driving a customer-focused mindset across your team and the wider fincrime organization. You are instrumental in fostering a high-performance, results-driven culture defined by strong ownership and accountability. This involves building and nurturing high-performing teams that value knowledge sharing, continuous learning, and adaptability in our change-oriented environment. Fincrime Operations Team Lead demonstrates strong capabilities in timely conflict resolution and fosters open communication and guides effective mediation to ensure a positive working environment. You should be visible and actively engaged in team management. Your focus is on unifying the team behind shared goals (and wider FinCrime/servicing strategies) and driving collective actions.

-
People management

Coach and develop a strong team of FinCrime Operations Analysts or Specialists with varying levels of experience, providing tailored guidance, and taking swift, decisive action to manage performance issues effectively, ensuring sustained excellence and growth. Provide regular, constructive, and actionable feedback to your direct reports. Coach and mentor team members to support their growth, develop their skills, and help them reach their full potential. Design and manage performance or development plans in identified areas. Conduct career map check-ins and make recommendations for demotions, promotions, salary raises, and other role related decisions.

-
Operational management

You will oversee the daily operations of the team, ensuring adherence to relevant regulations and internal policies and processes. Identify and propose opportunities for process and tooling improvements. Collaborate with central functions and other operational teams as needed to increase operational efficiency or to ensure effective cross-team collaboration on joint initiatives. Provide guidance and support on complex, high-risk cases and escalations. Be on top of timely admin related tasks including but not limited to scheduling, training, hiring, interviewing, organising team activities, and others.

-
Performance management

Measure team and individual KPIs and ensure performance targets and quality standards are consistently met while maintaining focus on customer experience and adherence to internal guidelines. Drive high-quality results for both the team and individuals, continuously enhancing overall quality outcomes. Conduct timely quality reviews, ensuring high decision accuracy and effectively communicate the importance of quality assurance. Conduct regular and impactful one on one coaching sessions (usually on a weekly or biweekly basis), provide clear and actionable feedback. Ensure tasks are managed timely and aligned with the team’s goals. Run team meetings to ensure that your team is kept up to date with the latest information, share best practices and enhance overall team spirit. Addresses underperformance promptly through coaching and setting SMART goals, and ensures all interventions are well-documented. Understand and be able to articulate how to move key metrics at team and individual level through efficient performance and task management.

-
Expertise sharing

Be a subject matter expert in financial crime areas with the ability to obtain and maintain sufficient subject matter expertise required to train, develop and coach your team. Maintain a comprehensive understanding of our regulatory obligations, internal policies, domain-specific processes and best practices. Apply a risk-based approach to deterring and preventing money laundering and financial crime. Perform and support deep dives, understand root causes of problematic cases and propose solutions to senior leadership. Assist senior leadership with reviews and developing our processes, task management and in other operational areas as requested to ensure compliant and effective servicing function

-
Issue Management and Escalation

Escalate tooling or processing incidents, high-risk customer issues, control weaknesses, or other material problems to direct leadership in a timely and informative manner, following established protocols.

-
Planning and execution

Be accountable for driving your direct team's performance outcomes, ensuring key performance indicators (KPIs) are consistently met and enhanced. Possess strong knowledge of team processes and tooling, leveraging data to support initiative execution. This involves taking full ownership of your team's results, setting targets for improvement, and providing insights to stakeholders. Set and progress towards goals, adeptly identifying and resolving blockers or issues, whether performance or metric-related, to optimize output and results.

-
Stakeholder management and communication

Collaborate closely with stakeholders ensuring clear communication and coordination of actions. Your initiatives and reports are well documented and you choose the right platforms to communicate to a wider audience in a timely manner. The documentation has a clear scope and includes potential impact in different areas. You can communicate confidently with difficult stakeholders on varied operational or domain related topics. Proactively work on improving cross-team communication and collaboration, acting as the liaison between different layers of the organization and your own team. Employ impactful and inspiring communication skills, unifying individuals behind shared goals, and leverage strong presentation skills to convey vision and progress.

-
Other: Perform additional tasks as assigned by your lead, demonstrating adaptability and a proactive approach. This includes actively participating in meetings, trainings, workshops, and internal events to support broader team and company objectives.

Job Description

We're looking for an experienced Senior Product Engineer to join the Risk & Control Governance team / Risk Assessment Group. You'll be instrumental in building the governance, assurance, and data foundations that ensure every risk decision at Wise is consistent, explainable, auditable, and continuously monitored.

This role works at the intersection of the Risk API platform, Product, and Financial Crime (FinCrime) teams — offering a unique opportunity to build the systems that give Wise confidence in every risk assessment it operates at scale.

You will be the driving force behind the platform's trustworthiness and integrity, focusing on:

-
Data Governance: Building and maintaining data ownership, lineage, and quality monitoring systems that ensure every risk decision is powered by trusted data.

-
Control Assurance: Designing continuous monitoring and validation systems that verify controls perform as intended — including trigger validation, drift detection, coverage analysis, and control health scoring.

-
Auditability & Explainability: Implementing end-to-end audit trails, change history tracking, and explainability tooling that enables one-click regulatory evidence generation.

-
Scalable Solutions: Designing robust, high-throughput solutions that handle large volumes of data and can be quickly understood and scaled across multiple distinct risk domains.

What will you be working on?

You will join the team at a pivotal moment, with your contributions being immediately visible and critical to the success of the entire Risk Assessment platform's governance layer.

The core challenge for the team — and your immediate focus — is to build the assurance and governance foundations that the platform currently lacks, ensuring every control can answer: Was the right trigger used? Was the right data available? Was the right decision made? Is the control still effective?

Your immediate impact will be to:

-
Build Data Trust: Implement data quality monitoring, data contracts, and lineage tracking that give the organisation full traceability from risk decisions back to source data.

-
Deliver Continuous Assurance: Design and build automated monitoring systems that continuously validate control effectiveness — detecting drift, false positives/negatives, and coverage gaps before they become incidents.

-
Enable Auditability: Create audit trail infrastructure and explainability tooling that dramatically reduces the effort required for regulatory reporting and compliance evidence generation.

-
Integrate with Risk API: Work closely with the Risk API team to embed governance and assurance capabilities into the core platform, ensuring clean integration points and shared data contracts.

Wise Platform Verification supports customers who access Wise through our partners. The domain spans different partner models, markets and operational routes. Parts of it are still difficult to measure and rely on fragmented or manual processes. This role will help the team build a reliable view of performance, identify the highest-value problems and establish better ways of working. When these flows are unclear or manual, partners can face delays, customers can hit avoidable friction, operations teams carry unnecessary work, and controls become harder to audit.

The team is building a more scalable verification model for Wise Platform: explicit requirements, better control monitoring, clearer operational flows, stronger automation, and partner-ready processes that can grow with Wise Platform.

About The Role

We are looking for an Implementation Manager to bring analytical rigour and process discipline to Wise Platform Verification. You will use data to understand how verification works across partners, identify the biggest sources of friction and operational cost, and lead improvements from diagnosis through implementation and measurement.

Your mission is to turn complex partner-verification problems into measurable implementation plans, trusted metrics, clear operating models, repeatable rollout playbooks, and automation opportunities. You will work across Product, Engineering, Analytics, Product Compliance, Risk, Partner Due Diligence and Operations teams, regional teams, and partner-facing teams to make sure verification changes launch safely, work operationally, and are measured after release.

This is not a coordinator-only role. You will create structure where it does not exist yet: map processes, define KPIs, identify root causes, challenge data quality, build launch scorecards, design operating cadences, and help move manual workflows toward automation.

What you will own

-
Map Wise Platform verification processes end to end, including partner models, control triggers, evidence flows, operational routing, RFIs, exceptions, and recovery paths.

-
Identify process and automation opportunities that reduce manual review, avoidable partner RFIs, misrouting, operational rework, and partner/customer disruption.

-
Define implementation plans for high-priority verification changes, including scope, owners, milestones, risks, launch gates, runbooks, training, adoption, monitoring, and escalation paths.

-
Build trusted KPI definitions, dashboards, launch scorecards, and weekly/monthly performance narratives that help the team make decisions.

-
Partner with Analytics and Data Science to validate data quality, segment impact, size populations, measure outcomes, and distinguish true performance changes from reporting or process artifacts.

-
Partner with Engineering to turn operational needs into implementable requirements while understanding technical constraints, dependencies, rollout paths, and migration risks.

-
Partner with Product Compliance, Risk, and Ops to make sure process changes meet control objectives, remain auditable, and work for the teams reviewing cases.

-
Support automation and process migration work, including moving fragile manual processes and legacy workflows toward scalable product or platform patterns.

-
Lead root-cause analysis for operational issues and partner-impacting verification pain points, then track fixes to closure and prevent recurrence through standards, monitoring, and documentation.

What success looks like in the first 6-12 months:

-
WPV has clearer process maps and ownership for the highest-impact partner verification workflows.

-
High-priority process changes launch with implementation plans, metrics, launch gates, runbooks, monitoring, and adoption tracking.

-
Manual review and partner RFI pain points are sized, prioritised, and converted into a practical automation or process-improvement backlog.

-
Partner Due Diligence, Operations, and partner-facing teams have clearer routing, context, escalation paths, and feedback loops.

-
The team can trust its core operating metrics and use them for prioritisation, launch readiness, and post-launch learning.

-
Operational incidents and recurring process issues lead to documented root causes, owners, fixes, and prevention mechanisms.

-
Legacy process or service ownership issues are mapped and sequenced with clear migration or handover plans.

This role gives you the opportunity to:

-
Work on one of the most important scaling problems for Wise Platform.

-
Build the operating system for partner verification across product, engineering, compliance, risk, data, and operations.

-
Improve how partners and their customers move through verification, while keeping controls robust and auditable.

-
Turn manual and fragmented workflows into measurable, repeatable, automatable processes.

-
Become an expert in partner verification, operational automation, risk controls, and platform-scale implementation.

Your Mission: Fraud and financial crime do not originate at Wise; they are conceptualized, tested, and commercialized within external threat-actor ecosystems long before they target our platform. Your mission is to establish a proactive presence in these spaces. By distinguishing critical intelligence from noise and disinformation, you will refine the ICF into a highly sophisticated instrument. Through OSINT, industry collaboration, and the direct monitoring of adversarial environments, you will convert raw data into actionable intelligence, serving as the primary radar for the TIU and Wise’s representative within the broader industry.

Key Responsibilities

-
Framework Operation: Manage and operate the ICF on a continuous basis, filtering out irrelevant data and contextualizing discoveries to deliver high-fidelity, actionable threat intelligence to the TIU and broader Wise business units.

-
Strategic Roadmap Ownership: Drive the end-to-end evolution of the collections roadmap, integrating new data sources and expanding capabilities across OSINT, deep/dark web monitoring, and closed social media networks.

-
Cross-Functional Enablement: Support the Analytical and Investigative functions of the TIU, alongside various internal teams, by translating intelligence into proactive defense mechanisms against fraud and financial crime.

-
Adversarial Monitoring: Monitor threat actors within their native environments—including fraud-as-a-service marketplaces, restricted forums, and encrypted messaging channels—to identify emerging tactics, techniques, and typologies (TTPs).

-
Requirements Gathering: Partner with internal stakeholders across Wise to understand their specific threat intelligence requirements and continuously optimize the ICF to meet those needs.

-
Industry Representation: Serve as a primary representative for Wise within industry working groups and public-private partnerships, identifying collaborative intelligence-sharing opportunities to combat systemic threats.

jobs.title: Senior Fullstack Engineer - Customer Risk Assessment
jobs.description:

More about our mission and what we offer.

At Wise, we’re on a mission to make financial services faster, simpler, and more accessible for everyone. But to achieve our mission, we also need to safeguard our platform against financial crime and ensure our customers' money is safe.

For our customers, using Wise is as simple as sending money from A to B. Yet behind our app and website is a complex engine that must navigate strict regulatory requirements worldwide. The Customer Risk Assessment team is at the absolute core of this effort. We are building the centralized platform that gives Wise deep visibility into any customer and their associated financial crime (fincrime) risk. By tying together all fincrime topologies into a unified view, we empower teams to make fast, accurate decisions.

Your mission will be to help build out this centralized platform, tying complex risk signals together while also owning the common components of risk mitigation. You will directly impact how Wise scales its compliance operations, enabling us to move with speed and confidence without ever compromising on the safety of our customers.

How we work:

We’re a cross-functional team of backend and frontend engineers working hand-in-hand with Product Managers, Analysts, and Designers. Collaboration is at the heart of what we do. We value ownership, open feedback, and a commitment to building stable, scalable systems while embracing fast-paced learning and iteration.

We operate with a belief in automation, programmatic implementation, and reusable design. We’re looking for engineers who can step back and think holistically about the entire fincrime ecosystem, but also follow through and help implement the design. You won't just be handed a list of Jira tickets; you will be expected to understand the underlying problems, challenge the proposed solutions, and propose simple, effective solutions that protect our customers' money.

What will you be working on?:

You’ll be having a real-world impact by building the systems that enable Wise to evaluate customer risk globally. Specifically, you will:

-
Build the full stack: Design, develop, and deploy resilient backend microservices in Java (Spring Boot) and build intuitive, accessible frontends using React and TypeScript.

-
Create a 360-degree risk view: Build the centralized tools that aggregate data across multiple fincrime topologies, giving our teams full visibility into customer risk profiles.

-
Drive risk mitigation: Own and develop the common components of our risk mitigation handling, ensuring our Servicing Agents have scalable, standardized workflows.

-
Scale operations: Break down complex bottlenecks in our servicing and compliance processes, delivering adaptable platform solutions that other Wise product teams can evolve to fit their specific needs.

-
Take ownership: Take full ownership of the product journey—from identifying a problem and empathizing with stakeholders, to creating an execution plan and shipping it to production.

Solid Backend Experience: You have a strong engineering background ideally in Java (familiarity with the Spring Boot stack) with years of experience putting scalable microservices into production and maintaining them in a cloud-based environment.

Frontend Skills: You have experience building performant, responsive web applications using React and TypeScript/JavaScript.

-
High Coding Standards: You are well-versed in writing clean, scalable, and testable code. You understand test coverage best practices, the test pyramid concept, and the value of code reviews.

-
Systems Architecture Knowledge: You have experience designing and implementing distributed, concurrent systems and understand the tradeoffs between stateful/stateless and synchronous/asynchronous architectures.

Product Mindset: You have the ability to break down complex projects into incremental milestones that deliver immediate customer value. The customer is at the heart of everything you do, and this empathy drives your decisions.

Great Communication: You thrive in a collaborative environment and can articulate complex, technical concepts to a non-technical audience or distributed cross-functional peers.

jobs.title: Lead Data Scientist - Pricing
jobs.description:
Wise is a global technology company, building the best way to move and manage the world’s money.

Min fees. Max ease. Full speed.

For everyone, everywhere.

More about our mission and what we offer.

We’re looking for a Lead Data Scientist to join our Pricing team in London.

This is a rare chance to shape how Wise prices cross-border money transfers — using data, machine learning and experimentation to keep pushing prices down while staying sustainable. What you build will have a direct impact on Wise’s mission and the millions of customers who rely on us for fair, transparent pricing

About the Role:

We are seeking a skilled and detail-oriented Data Scientist to help us develop a data-driven approach to pricing strategy and execution in a highly competitive remittance market.

As part of this team, you will leverage advanced analytics, machine learning, causal inference and robust experimentation to help Wise push price down, deepen our understanding of customers, and maintain a competitive edge. You will partner closely with the Pricing analytics and engineering teams, Pricing Product, FP&A, Commercial Directors and senior leadership — turning complex data into pricing decisions that move the business.

Here’s how you’ll be contributing:

-
Pricing Experimentation Framework

-
Design, build and run a robust framework for testing pricing structures, fee levels and promotional offers across corridors and customer segments.

-
Define key metrics, significance levels and reporting; apply causal inference to isolate the true impact of price changes.

-
Automate reporting and insight generation so pricing hypotheses can be tested scientifically and at scale.

-
Price Elasticity & Revenue Modelling

-
Partner with the Growth team to adapt price-elasticity insights into the core repricing framework.

-
Forecast the impact of price changes on demand, volume and revenue, and quantify the trade-offs.

-
Optimise pricing for different segments based on their sensitivity, and validate predictions against experimental data.

-
Automation & Data Infrastructure

-
Build data pipelines and monitoring that make accurate, timely pricing data accessible.

-
Reduce manual effort in pricing analysis and monitoring through automation.

-
Ensure data integrity through robust validation, and share best practices across the team.

-
Customer Contact Analysis

-
Apply machine learning to classify and analyse pricing-related customer support contacts (tickets, chats, calls).

-
Surface common pain points and confusion (e.g. “fee too high”, “confusing fee structure”) and emerging concerns.

-
Provide actionable insights to Product and Operations to reduce friction and simplify fee structures.

jobs.description:

We’re looking for an experienced Data Scientist to join our Customer Support team in London, working as part of a team based across London and Budapest.

You’ll help us understand how well our customer support experience is working, identify the biggest opportunities for improvement, and shape the path towards greater automation.

This is an analytical Data Science role with a strong product focus. You’ll use customer, conversational and operational data to measure service quality, diagnose issues, propose solutions and evaluate whether they improve outcomes. A key part of the role is simplifying complex customer journeys and operational systems into clear, tractable problems the team can act on.

You’ll work closely with Product, Design, Operations and Engineering to build a shared understanding of how the system works and turn insight into action.no

What you’ll do

Measure and diagnose

-
Build a clear, data-driven understanding of customer support quality across human and automated channels.

-
Design metrics that reflect meaningful customer outcomes, including resolution quality, customer effort, process adherence, consistency, fairness, durability of resolution and cost effectiveness.

-
Identify the root causes of issues by combining machine learning, statistical methods and domain expertise from colleagues to understand what genuinely drives customer outcomes.

Identify and test solutions

-
Turn analytical insight into concrete proposals to improve the customer experience, including product changes, process improvements, automation and better human support.

-
Quantify the potential impact and value of opportunities to help the team prioritise where to invest.

-
Design and analyse experiments to determine whether proposed changes genuinely improve customer and business outcomes.

-
Use statistical modelling and causal inference where controlled experiments are not practical.

Shape the automation strategy

-
Determine the right intervention for different customer problems — whether they should be automated, augmented by AI, handled by people or prevented altogether.

-
Test and evaluate interventions to understand their impact on customer outcomes, operational effectiveness and cost.

-
Shape the long-term automation capability roadmap, identifying what we should build next to maximise the value delivered over time.
jobs.requirements_raw:
What we’re looking for

Essential

-
An ability to simplify complex systems and ambiguous problems into clear hypotheses, useful abstractions and tractable analytical questions.

-
Strong analytical judgement, with the ability to get to a useful answer quickly, refine it iteratively, and know when the evidence is sufficient to support a decision.

-
Strong SQL and Python skills, with experience working with large, complex and imperfect datasets.

-
Strong grounding in statistical analysis (e.g., classical ANOVA, non-parametric uncertainty quantification, Bayesian estimation) and causal inference, with experience designing both controlled experiments and observational studies.

-
Experience applying machine learning, statistical modelling, NLP and LLM-based techniques to analyse customer behaviour and conversational data, diagnose root causes and identify the drivers of outcomes.

-
Experience designing measurement frameworks for complex customer journeys and evaluating the impact of interventions.

-
Strong product and business judgement, with a track record of using Data Science to influence important business decisions and drive measurable impact.

Preferred

-
Experience working on customer-facing products, ideally in customer support, customer operations or another high-volume service environment.

-
Experience evaluating the impact of automation or AI-powered customer experiences.

-
Experience applying predictive or behavioural modelling to support product or operational decision-making.

-
Experience working with sensitive customer data in environments with strong security, privacy or compliance requirements.

-
Experience combining quantitative analysis with qualitative or expert insight to solve complex problems.

-
Familiarity with modern analytics and machine learning tooling in a cloud environment such as AWS.

What success looks like

Success in this role means making a complex customer support system understandable enough that the team can make better decisions about it.

You’ll create clear ways of thinking about customer support quality, identify the biggest opportunities to improve outcomes, and turn those insights into concrete interventions that can be tested and measured.

Over time, you’ll help us make better decisions about where to automate, where to invest in human support, and which new capabilities to build — creating a support model that delivers more value to customers while becoming increasingly effective and scalable.

You’ll work closely with Product, Operations, Legal, Risk, Engineering, and Analytics while bringing clear, credible second-line challenge.

Your mission:

Help Wise build a testing program that is rigorous, practical, data-led, and focused on real customer outcomes. You will provide independent assurance over non-FinCrime regulatory risks in North America and turn complex obligations, production evidence, and operational signals into clear conclusions and actions.

You’ll work alongside a Financial Crime testing counterpart and a separate monitoring-oversight lead. Your primary lane is independent regulatory testing: you will not own routine 1LOD monitoring or the overall monitoring framework, although you may provide quality assurance or challenge over related monitoring outputs.

What You’ll Be Doing

-
Plan and execute risk-based regulatory testing and remediation-validation reviews from scope through final report.

-
Translate regulatory obligations and customer-outcome risks into precise control questions, populations, evidence requirements, test procedures, and failure criteria.

-
Test both control design and operating effectiveness, including whether controls work consistently in production and whether customer remediation is complete and reproducible.

-
Define and reconcile complete testing populations before sampling; use data and analytics to stratify risk, identify exceptions, and support defensible conclusions.

-
Review end-to-end processes that cross Product, Operations, technology, data, partner, and legal-entity boundaries.

-
Assess U.S. consumer-protection and payments requirements, including areas such as Regulation E, UDAAP/UDAP, E-SIGN, complaints, disclosures, customer communications, scams and restrictions, and state money-transmission obligations.

-
Evaluate state prudential and customer-funds controls where relevant, including safeguarding, permissible investments, liability-to-asset reconciliation, shortfalls, and selected regulatory-reporting evidence.

-
Write clear workpapers, issues, remediation-validation conclusions, and management reports that distinguish evidence, regulatory judgment, customer impact, and inference.

-
Challenge control owners and senior stakeholders constructively, agree practical corrective actions, and preserve independent second-line judgment.

-
Use Internal Audit, Group, first-line, or external-review evidence thoughtfully, relying only where the entity, population, period, procedure, result, and retained evidence support the specific assurance objective.

-
Support regulatory examinations, audits, partner due diligence, risk assessments, and governance reporting with accurate, well-organized testing evidence when needed.

-
Contribute to the continued development of NorthAm CMT methodology, templates, data use, quality standards, and reporting.
jobs.requirements_raw:
- You have substantial hands-on experience in compliance testing, internal audit, regulatory assurance, remediation validation, or a closely related independent-review role within financial services, payments, banking, an MSB, fintech, or a relevant consultancy.

-
You have strong working knowledge of U.S. consumer-protection and payments requirements and meaningful depth in several of Regulation E, UDAAP/UDAP, E-SIGN, complaints, disclosures, customer communications, state money-transmission, or safeguarding/prudential topics.

-
You can independently turn a broad risk into a bounded, defensible review with a clear objective, population, evidence plan, methodology, and conclusion.

-
You are comfortable working with data. You do not need to be a data scientist, but you can frame the right questions, challenge lineage and quality, reconcile populations, interpret exceptions, and partner effectively with analysts.

-
You distinguish documentation from implementation, implementation from operating effectiveness, and a clean test result from complete remediation closure.

-
You write clearly and concisely and can explain complex testing results to senior leaders and cross-functional teams.

-
You can challenge with evidence, stay practical, and build trust without becoming the owner of the controls you assess.

-
You care about customer outcomes and are curious about how systems and processes actually behave in production.

-
You are comfortable operating in a changing environment and can manage several dependencies without losing rigor or momentum.

-
You are legally authorized to work in the United States, subject to the work-authorization and visa language confirmed for the requisition.

Nice to haves:

-
Experience at a payments company, neobank, bank, MSB, remittance provider, platform/embedded-finance business, or high-growth fintech.

-
Experience with state money-transmitter licensing, NMLS, regulatory reporting, safeguarding, permissible investments, outstanding transmission liabilities, net-worth, surety, or other prudential obligations.

-
Experience testing partner or third-party handoffs, bank-partner models, customer-remedy processes, disclosures, electronic consent, complaints, scams, restrictions, or funds access.

-
Experience with regulatory exams, consent orders, MRAs/MRIAs, audit findings, issue validation, or significant remediation programs.

-
Experience with SQL, Snowflake, Lightdash, Looker, Tableau, Power BI, Excel, Jira, Confluence, GitHub, AuditBoard/Optro, Archer, or comparable analytics and workflow tools.

-
J.D., CRCM, CPA, CIA, CISA, CAMS, or a comparable qualification. We value demonstrated judgment and experience over any single credential.

A bit about you:

-
You ask what population and customer outcome a control is meant to protect before you ask how many samples to select.

-
You follow evidence across systems and team boundaries and do not stop at a policy, attestation, or dashboard when production proof is available.

-
You are precise about the boundary of your conclusion and transparent about what the review did not test.

-
You enjoy solving difficult problems with people from different disciplines and can turn challenge into practical improvement.

-
You bring ownership, integrity, curiosity, resilience, and good judgment under pressure.

-
Some travel to NYC, and potentially London for global compliance collaboration, may be required.

jobs.title: Account Manager - Payouts
jobs.description:
Wise is a global technology company, building the best way to move and manage the world’s money.

Min fees. Max ease. Full speed.

Whether people and businesses are sending money to another country, spending abroad, or making and receiving international payments, Wise is on a mission to make their lives easier and save them money.

As part of our team, you will be helping us create an entirely new network for the world's money.

For everyone, everywhere.

More about our mission and what we offer.

Wise Platform powers cross-border payments for banks, enterprise corporations, and global tech platforms. The Payouts team specifically serves high-volume enterprise clients—such as creator economy platforms, content licensing firms, and gig-economy businesses—that rely on Wise’s API infrastructure to send funds globally at scale.

As one of the first three hires on this newly formed team, you will own the entire post-sale lifecycle for North American enterprise accounts. You will be responsible for driving partner onboarding, ensuring smooth API integrations, maintaining account health, and proactively driving net revenue expansion through corridor, currency, and volume growth. In addition to client-facing duties, you will build the foundational account management playbook, escalation paths, and partner health frameworks for this business line.

Key Responsibilities:

1. Partner Onboarding & Go-Live (30%)

-
Partner with Pre-Sales and Implementation teams to project-manage newly signed enterprise accounts from contract execution to first successful payout run.

-
Ensure flawless technical go-lives to rapidly transition signed contract value into active processing volume.

2. Account Expansion & Revenue Growth (30%)

-
Own net revenue retention and expansion targets across your portfolio, driving adoption of new payment corridors, currencies, payout flows, and additional business units.

-
Translate pre-sale business cases into post-sale operational reality, actively growing volume month-over-month.

3. Technical Relationship Management & Portfolio Health (20%)

-
Serve as the primary, hands-on point of contact for live enterprise partners (e.g., creator platforms, marketplaces, gig-economy firms).

-
Act as a first-line technical resource to triage API batch failures, webhook errors, and settlement discrepancies directly with partner engineering teams before escalating to internal engineering.

-
Monitor transaction volume metrics continuously to identify usage anomalies, operational risks, or drop-offs ahead of formal account reviews.

4. Function Building & Operational Excellence (10%)

-
Design, test, and implement foundational post-sale processes, including client onboarding playbooks, account health scoring models, QBR formats, and internal escalation paths.

-
Collaborate cross-functionally with Global Wise Platform teams across Technical Support, Compliance, Pricing, and Product to optimize client experience and workflow efficiency.

5. Risk & Compliance Monitoring (10%)

-
Monitor evolving partner business models and payment flows to identify potential regulatory or compliance shifts, partnering with internal Compliance teams to adjust operational setups as needed.
jobs.requirements_raw:
-
Experience: 4+ years of post-sale account management, customer success, or partner management experience in payments, fintech, or technical API infrastructure.

-
Proven Track Record: Demonstrated experience meeting or exceeding quantified expansion and net revenue growth metrics (not solely customer satisfaction/NPS scores).

-
Technical Aptitude: Clear understanding of API and payment infrastructure concepts; able to accurately scope and diagnose client technical issues to drive quick resolution with internal engineering and product teams.

-
Builder Mindset: Strong comfort level with ambiguity, unstructured environments, and building operational playbooks from scratch.

-
Data Fluency: Proven capability using transactional data and client usage metrics to assess portfolio health and surface expansion opportunities.
